summary: This bill amends the Communications Act of 1934 to terminate the legal protections granted to online platforms under Section 230, making it ineffective after December 31, 2026.

scores.thoughts: This bill proposes to sunset Section 230 of the Communications Act of 1934, which provides immunity for online platforms from liability for third-party content and for their content moderation decisions. Repealing Section 230 would significantly increase the regulatory burden and potential liability for tech companies, pushing towards more oversight and data protection by forcing platforms to take more responsibility for content, which could indirectly affect how they handle user data and content moderation policies.
